page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-128 is an x86_64 general-purpose compute instance equipped with 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores powered by 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon processors. The processor topology allocates 2 threads per core and incorporates 54 MB of shared L3 cache, along with 48 KB of L1 data cache and 1 MB of L2 cache per core. Architectural instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware cryptography acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is configured with 512 GB of system RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled, and no hardware GPUs are present.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-core computing capability contrasted with median single-thread execution. The instance scores in the middle 50% for single-core benchmarks, reaching 1541.0 in Geekbench and 1844.49 in stress-ng. In contrast, parallelized performance places in the top tier, reflected by a multi-core stress-ng result of 120717.34, a PassMark CPU score of 84204.45, and a PassMark encryption score of 104777.43. The memory subsystem shows sustained throughput, recording 309.76 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth and 135.09 GB/sec in uncached write bandwidth. While small-to-medium language model prompt processing rates remain strong, token generation for large 70B parameter models is low at 2.7 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

The n2-standard-128 delivers high resource density for scenarios where multi-threaded execution can saturate 64 physical cores. Because filesystem capacity relies entirely on external network storage, I/O profiles must be balanced with appropriate persistent disk configurations. The instance profile is suited for high-concurrency database deployments, large distributed caching layers such as Redis, Clang-based software build environments, and parallel enterprise batch jobs.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-128 is a general-purpose compute instance featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs and 512 GB of RAM on a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon x86_64 architecture. The system provides 64 physical cores, 54 MB of L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction extensions. It includes no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, utilizing networked block storage for operating system and data volumes. Benchmarks establish strong multi-threaded compute and encryption performance, alongside an uncached read memory bandwidth exceeding 300 GB/sec. Single-threaded performance sits in the median range, and text generation on large language models remains constrained without dedicated acceleration. This instance is best aligned with large software compilation jobs, memory-backed caching tiers, enterprise database services, and high-concurrency static web workloads.
